episode_title: Bitcoin-Backed Loans Without KYC, Click by Click (Plus Boost Yield)
summary: Jules and Mira walk through opening a no-KYC bitcoin-backed loan on Chainflip Lending 2.0, covering why to borrow instead of sell, the three stablecoin markets, 80% max LTV, the new optional Boost yield on collateral, the six setup steps, and soft liquidation.
hook: Jules once pawned his guitar at a shop that was half pawn counter, half tanning bed, and had to watch the owner play it badly every day. Today, he and Mira walk through the opposite experience: borrowing stablecoins against native BTC with no KYC, no custodian, and collateral that can now earn Boost fees while your loan is open.
key_points: Why borrowing against BTC can beat selling it: you keep your position and avoid a sale
The three markets you can borrow from: USDT and USDC on Ethereum, plus USDT on TRON (launched June 2026)
How the 80% max LTV works, and why most borrowers stay well below it
What the new optional Lending 2.0 Boost yield toggle does with your collateral
The six steps to open a position, from connecting a wallet to 3 Bitcoin confirmations, plus how soft liquidation trims a position gradually

chapters.title: Cold open: Lonnie's Pawn and Tan
What you can borrow and the 80% line
Six steps to open a loan
Repaying, soft liquidation and the takeaway

lines.speaker: jules
lines.text: [grinning] Mira, have you ever pawned anything?

lines.speaker: mira
lines.text: [deadpan] No. Have you?

lines.speaker: jules
lines.text: Eighteen years old. Lonnie's Pawn and Tan, out by the grain elevator. Half pawn shop, half tanning bed. I pawned my electric guitar for eighty bucks to buy concert tickets.

lines.speaker: mira
lines.text: And?

lines.speaker: jules
lines.text: And every time I walked past, Lonnie was behind the counter playing my guitar. Badly. Boots up on the glass case.

lines.speaker: mira
lines.text: [half-laughing] Okay, that's actually today's episode. Welcome to Cross-Chain Daily, I'm Mira, that's Jules, and today we're walking through how to get a bitcoin-backed loan without K Y C, using Chainflip Lending two point oh.

lines.speaker: jules
lines.text: So, um, the Lonnie question. Why borrow against bitcoin at all? Why not just sell it?

lines.speaker: mira
lines.text: Selling means you exit your position, and you can trigger a taxable event. Borrowing means you get dollars and your bitcoin stays yours.

lines.speaker: jules
lines.text: Concert money, and I still own the guitar.

lines.speaker: mira
lines.text: Right. And people do this a lot. The article says outstanding crypto-backed loans hit seventy-three point five nine billion dollars by the third quarter of twenty twenty-five.

lines.speaker: jules
lines.text: Billion. With a B.

lines.speaker: mira
lines.text: Chainflip itself is much smaller, about one point two million dollars in active loans at the time of writing. But here's the big difference from Lonnie.

lines.speaker: jules
lines.text: Lonnie isn't holding it.

lines.speaker: mira
lines.text: No single person is holding it. You deposit native bitcoin, on the Bitcoin network, and it's secured by Chainflip's validator network. No wrapped token, no centralized custodian, no one entity controls the keys.

lines.speaker: jules
lines.text: So the guitar's in a case with a lock that, like, a whole committee has to open together. Nobody plays it on their lunch break.

lines.speaker: mira
lines.text: [amused] Close enough. And the article says that same setup has handled over six billion dollars in cumulative swap volume.

lines.speaker: jules
lines.text: Okay. What can I actually borrow?

lines.speaker: mira
lines.text: Three markets. U S D T on Ethereum, U S D C on Ethereum, and U S D T on TRON, which launched in June twenty twenty-six for lower gas costs. All three pull from the same collateral, so your bitcoin backs whichever one you pick.

lines.speaker: jules
lines.text: And how much? Because eighteen-year-old me would've asked for everything.

lines.speaker: mira
lines.text: Max loan-to-value is eighty percent. So one bitcoin worth sixty thousand dollars lets you borrow up to forty-eight thousand.

lines.speaker: jules
lines.text: [quick, cutting in] Which I should not do.

lines.speaker: mira
lines.text: Which most people don't. If bitcoin drops, your loan-to-value climbs toward that line. Interest is utilization-based, so the rate moves with how much of the pool is borrowed. Check the dashboard for current rates.

lines.speaker: jules
lines.text: Okay, the new thing. Boost yield.

lines.speaker: mira
lines.text: The big Lending two point oh change. Before, your collateral just sat there. Now there's an optional toggle so your bitcoin adds to swap liquidity when demand is high, and you earn a share of swap fees while your loan stays open.

lines.speaker: jules
lines.text: Wait. So it's like Lonnie renting my guitar to a wedding band on weekends and mailing me a cut.

lines.speaker: mira
lines.text: [grudgingly] Hmm. That half works. The guitar earns while it's in hock. But here you choose whether it goes out, and there's no Lonnie.

lines.speaker: jules
lines.text: Spreadsheet?

lines.speaker: mira
lines.text: [deadpan] I'm adding a second column. Half held up.

lines.speaker: jules
lines.text: [grinning] I'm making history. Okay, walk me through it. Click by click.

lines.speaker: mira
lines.text: Step one, go to lp dot chainflip dot io slash lending and connect an Ethereum wallet. MetaMask, Rabby, or anything that works with WalletConnect. You also need a Bitcoin wallet to send the collateral.

lines.speaker: jules
lines.text: Two wallets. Got it.

lines.speaker: mira
lines.text: Step two, hit Open Position and enter how much bitcoin you're depositing. It shows your max at eighty percent, a recommended safe amount below that, and in the October twenty twenty-six interface, a liquidation price estimate.

lines.speaker: jules
lines.text: Liquidation price. The number I stare at.

lines.speaker: mira
lines.text: The number you tape to your fridge. Step three, pick your stablecoin and type an amount. It updates live with your loan-to-value, estimated interest, and liquidation threshold.

lines.speaker: jules
lines.text: Step four's the wedding band toggle.

lines.speaker: mira
lines.text: Earn Boost yield on collateral. Optional, and the current estimated A P R shows right next to it.

lines.speaker: jules
lines.text: Then I send the bitcoin.

lines.speaker: mira
lines.text: Step five. Click Deposit Collateral, you get a unique Bitcoin deposit address, send from any wallet. It needs three Bitcoin confirmations before your collateral is active.

lines.speaker: jules
lines.text: Step six. Money.

lines.speaker: mira
lines.text: Stablecoins go to the address you specified. Ethereum tokens land in your connected wallet. For TRON U S D T, you enter a T R C twenty address during the borrow step.

lines.speaker: jules
lines.text: Don't paste your Ethereum address there.

lines.speaker: mira
lines.text: [dry] Please don't.

lines.speaker: jules
lines.text: I mean, paying it back? Lonnie gave me thirty days or the guitar was his.

lines.speaker: mira
lines.text: No lock-up here. Repay part or all of it any time. The dashboard shows your loan-to-value, accrued interest, and Boost earnings if you turned them on.

lines.speaker: jules
lines.text: And if bitcoin tanks?

lines.speaker: mira
lines.text: If your loan-to-value gets close to eighty percent, soft liquidation trims your position gradually instead of liquidating everything at once. That protects you from flash crashes and still makes sure lenders get repaid.

lines.speaker: jules
lines.text: So Lonnie sells one string at a time, not the whole guitar.

lines.speaker: mira
lines.text: [half-laughing] Fine, that's not bad. But the best plan is never getting near the line.

lines.speaker: jules
lines.text: Takeaway?

lines.speaker: mira
lines.text: You can borrow dollars against native bitcoin without selling it, without K Y C, and without handing it to a custodian, and now that collateral can earn Boost fees too. Just borrow way under eighty percent.

lines.speaker: jules
lines.text: The full article is linked in the show notes. Not financial advice, and please don't pawn your guitar.

lines.speaker: mira
lines.text: [amused] Stay native.

lore.note: At eighteen he pawned his electric guitar for $80 at Lonnie's Pawn and Tan (half pawn shop, half tanning bed, out by the grain elevator) to buy concert tickets, then watched Lonnie play it badly behind the counter with his boots on the glass case. Lonnie is his picture of a custodian holding your collateral.
Added a second column to her Jules-analogy spreadsheet, 'Half held up'; its first entry is Lonnie renting the pawned guitar to a wedding band (Boost yield on collateral).
His picture of soft liquidation: 'Lonnie sells one string at a time, not the whole guitar.' Mira admitted it's 'not bad.'
